attributes.description: Milestone 110 (task 545, flow 70). It names no product. Products project onto it from their own adapters (ciamProjectedFrom ownership).
attributes.purpose: Core neutral web access domain: protected web applications, their path resources and access rules (schema 776-798, classes 169-171), the projection helpers product importers use, the report, the planner check for apps left unprotected and cross-product move prerequisites, and the expressibility helper product checks and renders share.

attributes.name: read_config
attributes.purpose: Imported from a PingGateway configuration directory (config/ and routes/), its routes also projected onto the neutral protected-application layer (neutral.projection over the record after the import).

attributes.name: render_env
attributes.purpose: Adapter render_env: pinggateway/routes/<name>.json for every route except those whose protected application another role enforces in the environment (takeover.handed_over), plus a route for each protected application the environment has its gateways take over (takeover.takeover_routes).

attributes.name: check_routes
attributes.purpose: Planner check: routes that can't sign users in or whose backend role the target doesn't bind are blockers; fixed-backend routes are actions; fixes protect:pinggateway/<application> for protected applications the source enforces and nothing in the target would (when the target runs ig); else an ok line.

attributes.name: route_listeners
attributes.purpose: The ports an environment's gateways reach through routes that name a backend's service name role, and through the backends of the protected applications the environment has its gateways take over.

attributes.name: resource_id
attributes.purpose: The id Azure gives a resource of an azurerm type, as the importers read ids by their segments. Resources go under their resource group with namespace_of(type)/ARM_TYPES[type]/name. Children go under their parent (subnets under the network, flow logs under the network watcher, containers under the storage account, a load balancer's backend pools under the load balancer, so two load balancers' pools stay apart). Subscription-level ones go under the subscription: policy assignments, Defender pricings (by resource_type), the VA setting AzureServersSetting, role definitions and assignments by GUID. A type it doesn't place gets a synthetic id unique in the root.

attributes.name: imported
attributes.purpose: Imported of a Read: entries per kind (roles for hosts, integration and issuer for sessions, header contracts for mappings, held objects marked), groups per collection read, notices; plus the projection of the record's applications, resources and rules onto the neutral protected-application layer (neutral.projection over the record after the import).

attributes.name: entries_of
attributes.purpose: The record's entries of a collection, in record order (resources after their application); applications (and their resources) whose protected application another role enforces in the snapshot's view are left out (takeover.handed_over).

attributes.name: admin_api_files
attributes.purpose: {pingaccess/admin-api/requests.json: text} for an environment: per collection in order, the record's own objects' requests then those of the protected applications PingAccess takes over there (takeover.requests); nothing when there is nothing to render.

attributes.name: render_notes
attributes.purpose: Adapter.notes: render notes as data (unverified requests, environment-bound objects to create, withheld secrets, server profile and node files not rendered) and the taken-over applications' notes (takeover.takeover_notes: what PingAccess can't express, a client secret with no credential role).

attributes.name: check_pingaccess
attributes.purpose: Planner check: web sessions (client, issuer, token endpoint auth, PKCE, implicit login), withheld secrets, missing references, virtual host and site roles, engines in the target, fixed sites and unnamed headers (with fixes); and fixes protect:pa/<application> for protected applications the source enforces and nothing in the target would (when the target runs pa-engine).

attributes.name: site_listeners
attributes.purpose: Listeners the engines reach through sites naming a backend service name role, and through the backends of the protected applications the environment has PingAccess take over.

attributes.name: read_export
attributes.purpose: Importer siteminder/xps: Imported from XPSExport XML files (DOCTYPE refused, other releases refused): policy domains, realms, rules, policies, schemes, user directories, agents, integrations, header contracts and source objects; plus the projection of realms, rules and policies onto the neutral protected-application layer (neutral.projection over the record after the import).

attributes.name: app_dn
attributes.purpose: The DN of a protected application named name, under ou=protected-applications.

attributes.name: resource_dn
attributes.purpose: The DN of a path resource below its application's DN.

attributes.name: rule_dn
attributes.purpose: The DN of an access rule named name, under ou=access-rules,ou=protected-applications.

attributes.name: who
attributes.purpose: Split a ciamWho value into its kind and value ('' for authenticated).

attributes.name: protected_apps
attributes.purpose: Every protected application (ciamProtectedApp), in DN order.

attributes.name: access_rules
attributes.purpose: Every access rule (ciamAccessRule), in DN order.

attributes.name: path_resources
attributes.purpose: An application's path resources in evaluation order: those with ciamOrder first (lowest first), then the rest most specific first.

attributes.name: rules_of
attributes.purpose: The access rules an application or resource applies (ciamRuleRef), those the record holds, in the order named.

attributes.name: included
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true}, {"name": "rule", "type": "Entry", "required": true}, {"name": "seen", "type": "tuple", "description": "normalized DNs already visited", "required": false}]
attributes.purpose: A rule and every rule it includes (ciamIncludesRule), depth first, each once; a loop stops where it closes.

attributes.name: every_rule
attributes.purpose: Every access rule an application uses: its own, its resources', and those they include, each once, in order.

attributes.name: enforcer
attributes.purpose: The server role enforcing an application in an environment, as the environment sees it (its overrides applied).

attributes.name: enforced_by
attributes.purpose: The applications an environment has enforced by one of the given roles, as it sees them.

attributes.name: projected_from
attributes.purpose: The product entry a neutral entry was projected from, or None (an operator's, or the product entry is gone).

attributes.name: projected_within
attributes.purpose: Whether a neutral entry was projected from a product entry at or below a base DN (a product's own branch).

attributes.name: protected_app_rows
attributes.purpose: Report rows of the protected-applications report: name, base path, enforcing role, published names, backend, sign-on, integration, resource count, rules, projected-from, owners.

attributes.name: neutral_entry
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "dn", "type": "str", "required": true}, {"name": "oc", "type": "str", "description": "ciamProtectedApp, ciamPathResource or ciamAccessRule", "required": true}, {"name": "attrs", "type": "dict", "description": "{attribute: values} (None values dropped)", "required": true}]
attributes.purpose: Build a projected neutral entry of an object class; an attribute given no values is one the product says has none, an attribute left out one it says nothing about.

attributes.name: owns
attributes.purpose: Whether a projection may write an entry's DN: nothing holds it, or the record's entry there is projected from the same product entry.
attributes.returns: {"type": "bool", "description": "True when the projection owns the DN"}

attributes.name: differences
attributes.purpose: How a projection differs from the entry another product or an operator holds at its DN, over the attributes the projection says something about.

attributes.name: projected
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true}, {"name": "apps", "type": "tuple", "description": "((application entry, (resource entries...)), ...)", "required": true}, {"name": "rules", "type": "tuple[Entry]", "required": true}, {"name": "scopes", "type": "tuple[str]", "description": "the product DNs the import replaces", "required": true}, {"name": "label", "type": "str", "description": "what notices call the import", "required": true}]
attributes.purpose: The Projected of a product import: each owned application (with its resources, operator or other products' resources kept) and rule merged with the record (what the projection says replaces, the rest kept, the enforcing role set only where none is recorded); differences from entries it doesn't own as notices; projections of objects within the import's scopes no longer read removed.
attributes.returns: {"type": "Projected", "description": "containers, groups, notices to add to the product's Imported"}

attributes.name: after_import
attributes.purpose: The record as an Imported leaves it (each group's subtree made exactly its entries, its containers added), without the store's rules: what an importer projects its objects from.

attributes.name: merged_import
attributes.purpose: An Imported with a projection's containers, groups and notices added after the product's own.

attributes.name: served_by_issuer
attributes.purpose: The DN of the identity service whose OpenID Connect issuer is the given one (trailing slash aside), or None.

attributes.name: header_contracts
attributes.purpose: The DNs of the edge header contracts naming the given headers (case aside), in the names' order, each once.

attributes.name: pattern_as
attributes.purpose: A path pattern of one match kind written as another without changing what it matches: a prefix as a wildcard or regex, a wildcard as a regex; a regex as written.

attributes.name: expressible_who
attributes.purpose: Whether a product (its Capabilities) can test a ciamWho value (IPv6 networks only where it says so).

attributes.name: expressible_rule
attributes.purpose: Whether a product can render an access rule itself: not custom, a denial only where it renders denials, every subject testable.

attributes.name: losses
attributes.purpose: What a protected application uses that a product can't express, in order sign-on, session, resources, rules: a translated pattern info, sign-on or session limits it doesn't hold actions, rules it can't render blockers (the render would admit more).

attributes.name: protect_fix
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "m", "type": "EnvModel", "required": true}, {"name": "app", "type": "Entry", "required": true}, {"name": "role", "type": "str", "required": true}, {"name": "product", "type": "str", "description": "the product's name for the title", "required": true}, {"name": "adapter", "type": "str", "description": "the adapter name in the fix key", "required": true}]
attributes.purpose: The Fix having a product (its server role) protect an application in an environment: the environment's ciamOverride of ciamEnforcedByRole (key protect:<adapter>/<application>).

attributes.name: enforcer_header_fix
attributes.purpose: The Fix having a role set a header contract's header in an environment: its ciamOverride of ciamSetByRole (key enforcer-header:<contract>).

attributes.name: check_protected_apps
attributes.purpose: Planner check (area Web access): a blocker for an application the source enforces whose target enforcing role the target doesn't run; on a move to another product, blockers for missing or unbound published names, backend role and sign-in integration, and an action with fix enforcer-header for a header still set by another role; ok lines otherwise.

attributes.name: projection
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "view", "type": "Directory", "description": "the record as the import leaves it", "required": true}, {"name": "label", "type": "str", "description": "what notices call the import", "required": true}]
attributes.purpose: Projected of the record's PingAccess applications, resources and rules onto the neutral layer (applications enforced by pa-engine with base path, published service roles, site backend, web session sign-on/issuer/timeouts, identity mapping header contracts, policy rules; resources' patterns, methods, access; rules as attribute/scope/network tests, negate as deny, rule sets any/all, others custom).

attributes.name: taken_over
attributes.purpose: The neutral applications an environment has PingAccess's engines enforce that no paApplication projects.

attributes.name: handed_over
attributes.purpose: The DNs (lower-cased) of the PingAccess applications whose neutral application another role enforces, as a snapshot sees it.

attributes.name: requests
attributes.purpose: The Admin API requests of one collection for every application the environment has PingAccess take over (site, virtual hosts, identity mapping, web session, rules and rule sets, application, resources), each object once.

attributes.name: takeover_notes
attributes.purpose: Render notes for each taken-over application: what PingAccess can't express (express.losses with neutral.CAPABILITIES; rules it can't render are blockers) and a client secret with no credential role (blocker).

attributes.name: projection
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "description": "the record as the import leaves it", "required": true}]
attributes.purpose: Projected of the record's SiteMinder realms (applications <domain>-<realm> enforced by their agent's role, sign-on from the scheme type, timeouts, header contracts of granting policies), enabled rules (resources: wildcard/regex/prefix below the realm, HTTP methods, unprotected when ProtectAll is false, granting policies' rules) and enabled policies (access rules allow and -deny with group/user/filter/authenticated subjects, custom otherwise); event actions named in notices.

attributes.name: domain_of
attributes.purpose: The SiteMinder policy domain a realm, rule or policy is in (the entry below ou=realms or ou=policies of it).

attributes.name: granting
attributes.purpose: The enabled policies of a realm's domain granting one of its rules.

attributes.name: base_path
attributes.purpose: The base path a route's condition tests request.uri.path for (a literal prefix), or None.

attributes.name: app_source
attributes.purpose: The ciamProjectedFrom of a projected neutral application (the route's DN).

attributes.name: projection
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "description": "the record as the import leaves it", "required": true}]
attributes.purpose: Projected of the record's PingGateway routes: applications enforced by ig (base path from the condition, published service name from the host test, backend role and scheme, oidc sign-on through the client filter's integration and the issuer's identity service, session timeout as idle, HeaderFilter header contracts, ConditionEnforcementFilters as access rules), resources from AllowOnlyFilter rules (else one for every path) and ConditionalFilter-skipped anonymous paths.

attributes.name: taken_over
attributes.purpose: The neutral applications an environment has its gateways (ig) enforce that no route projects.

attributes.name: handed_over
attributes.purpose: The DNs (lower-cased) of the routes whose neutral application another role enforces, as a snapshot sees it.

attributes.name: route
attributes.purpose: The route of one taken-over application: condition (published hosts, base path), baseURI from the backend role, JwtSessionManager idle timeout, and a Chain of the sign-in (ConditionalFilter around AuthorizationCodeOAuth2ClientFilter skipping anonymous/unprotected paths), AllowOnlyFilter per resource, ConditionEnforcementFilter per rule, HeaderFilter for the header contracts, then ReverseProxyHandler.

attributes.name: takeover_notes
attributes.purpose: Render notes for each taken-over application (Adapter.notes): what PingGateway can't express (express.losses with neutral.CAPABILITIES) and where the sign-in's client secret comes from.

attributes.name: own_routes
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "files", "type": "dict", "required": true}, {"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "description": "the record as the environment sees it", "required": true}, {"name": "environment", "type": "str|None", "required": true}]
attributes.purpose: Adapter.reads_back prepare: the rendered gateway files without the routes made for taken-over applications.

attributes.name: takeover_routes
attributes.purpose: {pinggateway/routes/<application>.json: route} for every application the environment has its gateways take over.

attributes.name: own_requests
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "files", "type": "dict", "required": true}, {"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "description": "the record as the environment sees it", "required": true}, {"name": "environment", "type": "str|None", "required": true}]
attributes.purpose: Adapter.reads_back prepare: the rendered requests files as PingAccess's own entries render them: without the requests made for taken-over applications (the neutral layer's render) and with those of the applications another role enforces in the environment (left out of its render, still PingAccess's entries).

attributes.name: filters
attributes.purpose: Every filter (or heap object) of a type anywhere in a route, in document order.

attributes.description: What an enforcing product can express of the neutral protected-application layer: product name, match kinds, translated match kinds ((kind, as kind), ...), access modes, who-kinds, sign-on kinds, whether it renders denials, which of idle/max session limits it enforces, whether its network rules take IPv6.
attributes.name: Capabilities

attributes.description: One thing a product can't express of a protected application: severity info (translated), action (lost: someone decides) or blocker (a rule left out: the render admits more), and its text.
attributes.name: Loss

attributes.description: What a product importer adds to its Imported for its neutral projections: containers, groups (scope DN, entries; an empty group removes a stale projection) and notices.
attributes.name: Projected

attributes.description: Milestone 110 in full (description there; notes 3083, 3090, 3095). A neutral core layer for a protected web application (host/base path, enforcing server role, sign-on kind and served-by identity service, session timeouts), its path resources (pattern, match kind prefix|wildcard|regex, methods, access standard/anonymous/unprotected, order) and access rules (allow/deny, any/all, subject expressions), linked to ciamHeaderContract and integrations. PingAccess (arc .3.5), SiteMinder (arc .3.6) and PingGateway map onto it as importer-side projections, so the planner compares cross-product moves (SiteMinder -> PingAccess, PingAccess -> PingGateway) and the target product renders its policy from the source's. This changes what the record holds: the design (schema classes/attributes, where projections live, what the planner compares, what renders) goes to the master, who confers with the user, before coding.
attributes.name: Neutral protected web application layer (core + PingAccess, SiteMinder, PingGateway projections)

attributes.description: Neutral classes/attributes (core arc, assigned numbers), how PingAccess, SiteMinder and PingGateway project onto it, what the planner compares across products, what each product renders from it; master confers with the user before coding.

attributes.name: Core neutral layer

attributes.description: PingAccess, SiteMinder and PingGateway importers project onto the neutral layer; renders read from it where the design says.
attributes.name: Product projections

attributes.description: Cross-product move checks (SiteMinder -> PingAccess, PingAccess -> PingGateway) over the neutral layer, findings as data to the owning team.
